newsitem.title: Singapore: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals quiet, focus on sterling.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals quiet, focus on sterling.

text.p: * Regional currencies subdued with many players out for long weekend after May Day holiday and ahead of Japanese holiday on Monday. Focus on sterling after Labour's landslide win in British general election.
* Indonesian rupiah recovers from weak open but dollar seen supported on continuing anxiety over election campaign.
* Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar confined to narrow range on lack of fresh leads.
* Thai baht, interbank rate firm ahead long weekend. Forwards active on reports of problems with Finance One/Thai Danu merger.
Southeast Asian currencies made slow progress in thin markets on Friday as many players remained away after the May Day holiday and ahead of a Japanese holiday on Monday.

Dealers said trade was slow with attention focused on sterling after Labour's landslide election victory. Interest in the dollar/majors was subdued ahead of the U.S. non-farm payrolls report at 1230 GMT.
In Indonesia, the rupiah was off its opening lows but dealers said the dollar looked well supported on continuing anxiety about the election campaign.
Some dollar selling from Singapore players around the 2,434.50 level helped the rupiah recover to around 2,432.60/33.90 at 0420 GMT against an opening 2,434.5/35.5.
A local bank dealer in Jakarta said the dollar appeared to be well supported at the 2,432.0 level by domestic players in the face of relatively ample liquidity in the morning.
Dealers said the overall trend suggested operators were tending to go long on dollars due to underlying caution during the campaign for the May 29 general elections.
A Singapore dealer said the ample money market liquidity in Jakarta would also inhibit dollar selling.
Dealers said the forward market seemed to have been neglected in the past few days, suggesting speculation was on the increase.
"It's easier to get in and out from the market if you only get involved in the spot market," the Singapore dealer said.
In Thailand, demand for funds ahead of Monday's holiday pushed the interbank rate higher.
The baht was quoted at 26.105/26.110 to the dollar at 0420 GMT against 26.110-26.115 late on Wednesday. The market was closed on Thursday. The Bank of Thailand mid-rate was 26.09.
Dealers said the spot market was quiet but forwards rose on reports of problems with a proposed merger between Finance One and Thai Danu Bank.

Thai Danu Bank Plc earlier this year announced it was to merge with Finance One, Thailand's largest non-bank financial institution. Local newspapers reported on Thursday that the deal was in danger of collapse.
Elsewhere, the Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar were trapped in tight ranges as activity dwindled ahead of the weekend.
Kuala Lumpur dealers said the ringgit was supported by some short-covering while commercial buying of the ringgit against the Singapore dollar could also help the Malaysian unit.
"There's still a bit of short covering. The market is squaring off ahead of the weekend and jobs data," a dealer at a Malaysian bank said.
The ringgit was expected to trade within a 2.5080-2.5120 range to the U.S. dollar.
The Singapore dollar came up against U.S. dollar buying interest from U.S. names around the 1.4450 level but dealers said it was unlikely to weaken beyond 1.4480.
"People are taking profit from 1.4460 upwards. It's just range trade," one dealer said. The recent weakness of the local stock market was contributing to the Singapore dollar's soft tone, he added.
"A lot of foreign funds have interests in local stocks. And they've been getting out and flooding the market with Singapore dollars," he said.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
